order_description: Implantation of a hypoglossal nerve neurostimulator system (stimulation lead, pulse generator and respiratory sensor) for obstructive sleep apnea

candidates.title: Hypoglossal Nerve Stimulation for the Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea
Hypoglossal Nerve Stimulation for the Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea
Hypoglossal Nerve Stimulation for the Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea

selection_reason: All three candidates are the same HGNS policy from different MACs; L38398 (First Coast) describes the FDA-approved three-component system matching the ordered 64582 implant (stimulation lead, pulse generator, respiratory sensor), and the patient has severe OSA (AHI 32, central apneas 8%, SpO2 nadir 86%), CPAP intolerance despite mask and pressure changes, BMI 29.5 (under 40), no complete concentric palate collapse, and a surgeon evaluation with DISE, so the criteria appear to be met; any of the same-policy versions may be chosen.

criteria.policy_text: Beneficiary is 22 years of age or older
criteria.explanation: The sleep medicine note of 2026-12-29 and the otolaryngology note of 2027-01-23 both document a 32-year-old female. She is 32 at the planned implant on 2027-02-13, which satisfies the 22-year minimum.

criteria.policy_text: Body mass index (BMI) is less than 35 kg/m2
criteria.explanation: BMI was 29.5 kg/m2 on 2027-01-23, recorded in the observation and in the otolaryngology exam. This is below 35.

criteria.policy_text: A polysomnography (PSG) is performed within 24 months of first consultation for HGNS implant
criteria.explanation: An attended in-laboratory Type I polysomnography was performed on 2026-08-26 (report 2026-08-28). The first HGNS consultation was on 2026-12-29, about four months later and well within 24 months.

criteria.policy_text: Beneficiary has predominantly obstructive events (defined as central and mixed apneas less than 25% of the total AHI)
criteria.explanation: Central and mixed apneas were 8% of the total AHI on the 2026-08-27 study, which is below the 25% threshold.

criteria.policy_text: AHI is 15 to 65 events per hour
criteria.explanation: AHI was 32 events per hour on the 2026-08 polysomnography, which falls within 15 to 65.

criteria.policy_text: Beneficiary has documentation that demonstrates CPAP failure (defined as AHI greater than 15 despite CPAP usage) or CPAP intolerance (defined as less than 4 hours per night, 5 nights per week or the CPAP has been returned) including shared decision making that the patient was intolerant of CPAP despite consultation with a sleep expert
criteria.explanation: The alternatives are CPAP failure or CPAP intolerance. The record meets the intolerance alternative: average use was 2.6 hours on nights used (below 4 hours), and CPAP was used on only 12 of the last 30 nights (fewer than 5 nights per week). Residual AHI on CPAP was 5, so the AHI-failure alternative does not apply. Shared decision making about CPAP intolerance was documented by the sleep medicine physician on 2026-12-29 (R75) and again by the otolaryngologist on 2027-01-23 (R76), with the patient reported as intolerant despite mask and pressure changes.

criteria.policy_text: Absence of complete concentric collapse at the soft palate level as seen on a drug-induced sleep endoscopy (DISE) procedure
criteria.explanation: The 2027-02-13 DISE report states that the velum shows partial anteroposterior collapse with no complete concentric collapse.

criteria.policy_text: No other anatomical findings that would compromise performance of device (e.g., tonsil size 3 or 4 per standardized tonsillar hypertrophy grading scale)
criteria.explanation: Tonsils are size 1 on the Brodsky scale, the neck is supple without masses, and Mallampati is class II. The DISE shows partial lateral wall and tongue base collapse and no epiglottic collapse. None of these is described as compromising the device, and the implanting surgeon proceeded after evaluating them.

criteria.policy_text: HGNS is not reasonable and necessary when any listed contraindication is present (including central/mixed apneas over one-quarter of AHI, implanted devices, BMI of 35 or more, neuromuscular disease, hypoglossal palsy, severe pulmonary disease, pulmonary arterial hypertension, valvular disease, NYHA III/IV heart failure, recent MI or severe arrhythmia, uncontrolled hypertension, serious mental illness, nonrespiratory sleep disorders, pregnancy, MRI needs, inability to operate the remote, or conditions affecting upper airway neurological control)
criteria.explanation: No listed contraindication is documented as present. The otolaryngology contraindication screen on 2027-01-23 records no neuromuscular disease, hypoglossal palsy, severe pulmonary disease, pulmonary arterial hypertension, valve disease, heart failure, recent MI or severe arrhythmia, serious mental illness, other sleep disorder, pregnancy or planned pregnancy, implanted devices, anticipated MRI, or inability to operate the remote. Blood pressure was 105/83 and recorded as controlled, BMI is 29.5, and central/mixed apneas are 8%. The tubal ligation history (R7) does not indicate current pregnancy.

decision_explanation: Every applicable criterion is documented as met: age, BMI, timely PSG, predominantly obstructive events, AHI within range, CPAP intolerance with shared decision making, absence of complete concentric collapse on DISE, no compromising anatomy, and no listed contraindication. Provider credential, certification, accreditation and billing requirements were excluded as administrative.
